question: A 21-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 1-day history of right leg pain. The pain is worse while walking and improves when resting. Eight months ago, she was diagnosed with a pulmonary embolism and was started on warfarin. Anticoagulant therapy was discontinued two months ago. Her mother had systemic lupus erythematosus. On examination, her right calf is diffusely erythematous, swollen, and tender. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. On duplex ultrasonography, the right popliteal vein is not compressible. Laboratory studies show an elevated serum level of D-dimer and insensitivity to activated protein C. Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to show which of the following?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "History of pulmonary embolism" -> "Anticoagulant therapy with warfarin" -> "Discontinuation of anticoagulant therapy" -> "Increased risk of recurrent thrombosis" -> "Right leg pain, erythema, swelling, and tenderness" -> "Possible deep vein thrombosis (DVT)" -> "Duplex ultrasonography showing non-compressible right popliteal vein" -> "Likely diagnosis of DVT" -> "Further evaluation for underlying cause of DVT" -> "Possible genetic predisposition to thrombosis" -> "Investigation for inherited thrombophilia disorders" -> "Most likely to show mutation of coagulation factor V" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Elevated D-dimer levels" -> "Insensitivity to activated protein C" -> "Possible hypercoagulable state" -> "Increased risk of thrombosis" -> "Clinical presentation with right leg pain, erythema, swelling, and tenderness" -> "Suspicion of deep vein thrombosis (DVT)" -> "Duplex ultrasonography findings of non-compressible right popliteal vein" -> "Further evaluation for underlying cause of DVT" -> "Likely genetic predisposition to thrombosis" -> "Investigation for inherited thrombophilia disorders" -> "Most likely to show mutation of coagulation factor V" -> 75%
analysis: The patient's presentation with a history of pulmonary embolism, current leg pain, erythema, swelling, and tenderness in the right calf, along with a non-compressible right popliteal vein on ultrasound, elevated D-dimer, and insensitivity to activated protein C suggests a high likelihood of deep vein thrombosis (DVT). Given the family history of systemic lupus erythematosus, further evaluation is likely to reveal a mutation of coagulation factor V (Factor V Leiden mutation) as the most probable cause of her current condition.
